from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine a sphere, like a globe.",
            "Antipodal points are exactly opposite.",
            "Like Tokyo and the South Atlantic.",
            "They are mirrors through the center.",
            "Symmetry is built into our world."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Intuition of Antipodes", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup sphere and points
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3).set_shade_in_3d(True)
        # Using 2D projections for the 3D sphere representation for consistent positioning
        sphere_2d = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere_2d, 'C3')
        
        point_tokyo = Dot(color=WHITE).move_to(sphere_2d.point_at_angle(PI/4))
        point_atlantic = Dot(color=WHITE).move_to(sphere_2d.point_at_angle(PI/4 + PI))
        line = Line(point_tokyo.get_center(), point_atlantic.get_center(), color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere_2d))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(point_tokyo), FadeIn(point_atlantic))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(Indicate(point_tokyo, color=RED), Indicate(point_atlantic, color=RED))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(sphere_2d.animate.set_color(GREEN), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Transition: From Spheres to Necklaces", ["Now, let's talk about necklaces.", "Two thieves want a fair share.", "Can we cut fairly with beads?"])
        
        # Colors
        c_gold = "#FFD700"
        c_silver = "#C0C0C0"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C2')
        self.play(Create(circle))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        beads = VGroup()
        for i in range(20):
            color = c_gold if i < 10 else c_silver
            bead = Dot(radius=0.15, color=color)
            beads.add(bead)
        beads.arrange_in_grid(rows=1, buff=0).shift(beads.get_center()*-1).shift(self.grid['C2']) # Corrected approach
        beads.submobjects = [] # Clear for re-distribution
        for i, bead in enumerate(beads):
            angle = i * (2 * PI / 20)
            bead.move_to(self.grid['C2'] + 1.5 * (np.cos(angle) * RIGHT + np.sin(angle) * UP))
            beads.add(bead)
        self.play(FadeIn(beads))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        cut_line = Line(start=UP*0.5, end=DOWN*0.5, color=RED).rotate(PI/4)
        self.place_at_grid(cut_line, 'C2')
        self.play(Create(cut_line))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Solving the Necklace Problem", ["This is the Necklace Problem.", "K-types of beads need K-cuts.", "Borsuk-Ulam proves it is possible."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Represent a 2-colored necklace as a line of beads
        necklace = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.15, color=color, fill_opacity=1) 
                            for color in [RED, BLUE, RED, BLUE, BLUE, RED, BLUE, RED]])
        necklace.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(necklace, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(necklace))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Show cuts visually
        cut1 = Line(UP*0.3, DOWN*0.3, color=WHITE).next_to(necklace[2], RIGHT, buff=0.05)
        cut2 = Line(UP*0.3, DOWN*0.3, color=WHITE).next_to(necklace[5], RIGHT, buff=0.05)
        self.play(Create(cut1), Create(cut2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        formula = MathTex(r"f: S^k \to \mathbb{R}^k", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Why Symmetry Matters", [
            "Topology guarantees fairness in systems.",
            "Perfect balance is mathematically inevitable.",
            "Symmetry is fundamental to fairness."
        ])
        
        # Visuals
        symmetry_icon = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE).add(Line(LEFT*0.5, RIGHT*0.5, color=BLUE))
        balance_icon = VGroup(
            Triangle(color=WHITE).scale(0.5),
            Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE).shift(UP*0.2)
        )
        final_summary = VGroup(
            Text("Fairness", font_size=36, color=WHITE),
            Text("Guaranteed by Math", font_size=24, color=GRAY)
        ).arrange(DOWN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(symmetry_icon, 'B3')
        self.play(FadeIn(symmetry_icon))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_at_grid(balance_icon, 'D4')
        self.play(FadeIn(balance_icon))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_in_area(final_summary, 'E2', 'F5')
        self.play(Write(final_summary))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem: Fairness in a Necklace

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Intuition of Antipodes
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a sphere (S²) and antipodal points—pairs of points exactly opposite each other on the surface. Visualize this as the North and South poles, or any point (x, y, z) and its reflection (-x, -y, -z).
sections.example: An animation showing a globe where if you touch a spot in Tokyo, the antipodal point is deep in the Atlantic Ocean near Argentina.

sections.title: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem (The Core Concept)
sections.content: State the theorem: Any continuous function from an n-sphere to n-dimensional Euclidean space must map at least one pair of antipodal points to the same value. Use the 'Temperature/Pressure' analogy: there exist two opposite points on Earth with identical temperature and pressure.
sections.example: Visualizing a 2D map of Earth where two 'thermometers' are linked by a rigid bar; as you rotate the bar, they eventually hit two points of identical temperature.

sections.title: Transition: From Spheres to Necklaces
sections.content: Explain how the 'Stolen Necklace Problem' is a discrete combinatorial application of this topological theorem. We have a necklace with beads of different types (e.g., gold and silver) and need to cut it into pieces to distribute fairly among two thieves.
sections.example: Two thieves, Alice and Bob, have a string of 10 gold beads and 10 silver beads. They want to cut the string so both get exactly 5 gold and 5 silver beads.

sections.title: Application: Solving the Necklace Problem
sections.content: Demonstrate the theorem's power: If there are 'k' types of beads, the necklace can be split fairly using at most 'k' cuts. This transforms a complex search problem into a topological existence proof.
sections.example: An animation of a 2-colored necklace. As a slider moves, the necklace 'deforms' into a shape that satisfies the Borsuk-Ulam requirements, showing exactly where the cuts must be made to ensure an equal split.

sections.title: Conclusion: Why Symmetry Matters
sections.content: Summarize that Borsuk-Ulam is a 'fixed-point' style theorem that guarantees fairness in distributed systems. It shows that in any sufficiently complex system, perfect balance (symmetry) is not just possible—it is mathematically inevitable.
sections.example: A final visual showing the 'perfectly cut' necklace distributed between two animated characters, emphasizing that math provided the 'fair judge'.
